AUTHOR: Lopez-Vazquez
TITLE: Deep learning based deep-sea automatic image enhancement and animal species classification
REGION: Barkley Canyon Hydrates site (~870 m), NEPTUNE/ONC, NE Pacific, Canada
SPECIES: Sebastidae, Bathyagonus nigripinnis, Eptatretus stoutii (fish) plus Chionoecetes tanneri, Asteroidea, Bolinopsis infundibulum, Poralia rufescens, particles, objects, other species
DATA: Own still images from crawler 'Wally' (18 transects, Nov-Dec 2016, 1 Hz)
V_EV: Data collection: 'Imaging was performed at 1 Hz ... with illumination provided by two 33 W, 2000 m rated LED lamps.'; Hydrates site '~ 870 m depth'
D2: 80/20 train/test (enhancement and classification); classifiers evaluated by tenfold cross-validation
D_EV: Experimental design: 'All the selected classifiers were tested by tenfold cross-validation by considering that the elements of each class were distributed evenly in each fold'
R_EV: Data collection: 'a total of 18 imaging transects (i.e., 9 forth and 9 back) of ~ 30 m length were carried out between 2 November and 2 December 2016.'
C_EV: Classification metrics: 'Accuracy', 'AUROC', 'Loss', 'The confusion matrix' only; no score threshold, reject option or counting output
E_EV: Results: 'RF2 obtained an accuracy value of more than 0.75 and an AUROC value of almost 0.87.' (classification metrics only)
ARCH: Residual CNN autoencoder for enhancement; frame-difference detection; classifiers SVM, k-NN, DT, RF, CNN1-4, DNN1-4
METR: UIQM, UCIQE, SSIM, PSNR; accuracy, AUROC, loss, confusion matrix
NOTE: Image-quality metrics UIQM and UCIQE both reported (V5 coded UIQM; UCIQE also). Turbidity/sediment clouds described qualitatively only; performance compared across enhancement variants, not stratified by water condition (V6=N). Split: 80/20 and tenfold CV over samples from consecutive 1 Hz frames of the same transects; unit not separated by transect -> k-fold(image), D_ALL=N. Abstract's 'independent test data set' is just the held-out split. Detection by frame differencing but only classification evaluated, no score threshold -> C_ALL=NA (AUROC implies scores exist; verifier may prefer NR). Crawler (IOV) coded as ROV/AUV. Fish are 3 of 10 classes.
